Self-train YOLO

feature map first, then NV12

Chapter 2 Model Zoo, lesson 5: self-train YOLO—tune the quantization path with feature map first, then switch to NV12. Model is YOLO11n detect; dataset is the public mini-set coco128. Dual boards: X5 and S100. [Read] YOLO as yolo; feature map as a whole word; NV12 per handbook.

Leave able to ship this path

Self-train detect → feature map on both boards → then NV12 → one Sample frame.

02

yaml → feature map; full OE + one-frame infer on X5 and S100

NV12 + Sample

Why self-train. Weights are this lesson’s fine-tune; dataset is the public coco128 mini-set—not production data; full training finishes locally, then later export and board steps use those trained weights.
Train

YOLO11n · 40 epoch

This lesson uses coco128; command skeleton is repeatable—tune hypers from your run.

detect trainhost: ~/course_2-05
yolo detect train data=coco128.yaml \
model=yolo11n.pt epochs=40 imgsz=640 \
project=datasets/coco128_run/runs/detect \
name=selftrain

RDK Classroom 2-05
Part two: why every model starts with feature map, and get the conversion yaml right.
Principle

Every model first tunes with feature map

Once the full path works, then consider NV12 or RGB
RDK Classroom 2-05
Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · Why Feature Map First11 / 34
Left: jumping to NV12 or RGB forces cal through color and normalize—too many variables when the path fails. Right: feature map is the float32 input tensor fed to the network, matching the self-train ONNX domain of zero-to-one. Both boards share that numeric domain; only the container differs—X5 .rgbchw, S100 .npy. Compare with that board’s file; do not mix. This is a single-image input-domain loop, not an mAP or generalization accuracy cert. Once it works, switch to NV12 or RGB. [Read] feature map whole word; NV12 per handbook; YOLO as yolo.
Feature map

OE featuremap is not a mid-layer

Here featuremap = the float32 tensor fed straight into the network, matching the ONNX input.

  • ✓Cal tensors: float32 0..1 (X5 .rgbchw / S100 .npy)
  • ✓Matches real network input—easy ONNX↔quant compare
  • !Not a CNN mid-layer feature map; then change NV12/RGB protocol
RDK Classroom 2-05
Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · What FM Means12 / 34
OE featuremap is the float32 tensor fed straight into the network—not a CNN mid-layer. Cal matches real network input for compare; change the input protocol only after it works. [Read] feature map whole word.
rt · train

rt meets the edge · train is the input domain

train does not mean “train again”: it is the float model’s input domain; rt is what the board actually feeds.

  • →train_*: float model input (FM=featuremap; NV12 stage=rgb)
  • →rt_*: edge runtime input (FM=featuremap; NV12=nv12)
  • ✓Keep dtype/layout apart from color protocol: NV12 ≠ RGB layout
RDK Classroom 2-05
Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · Input Protocol13 / 34
Input protocol: train describes the float model input domain—not retraining; rt describes what the board actually feeds. In the feature-map stage both sides are featuremap; in the NV12 stage rt becomes nv12 and train becomes rgb. RGB and NV12 are different input protocols. See X5 / S OE docs.
conversion/

Same FM fields · same 0..1 domain

ptq_featuremap_{x5,s100}.yaml; both no_preprocess; both 0..1—X5 .rgbchw, S100 .npy.

ItemX5 FMS100 FM
YAMLptq_featuremap_x5ptq_featuremap_s100
marchbayes-enash-e
rt/train · normfeaturemap · no_ppfeaturemap · no_pp
calrgbchw 0..1npy 0..1
RDK Classroom 2-05
Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · YAML · FM Side-by-side14 / 34
FM side-by-side: both boards use featuremap and no_preprocess with the same 0..1 domain; they differ in march and file container—X5 rgbchw, S100 npy. Self-train ONNX expects 0..1. This is a single-image input-domain loop, not an mAP cert. [Read] bayes-e / nash-e = arch name + pause + letter.
YAML

Start from conversion · edit fields

Trunk stays ultralytics_yolo/conversion; fields also compare yolo26_depth / efficient_sam.

input_parameters (excerpt)ptq_featuremap_x5.yaml
input_type_rt: 'featuremap'
input_type_train: 'featuremap'
input_layout_train/rt: 'NCHW'
norm_type: 'no_preprocess'
Cal

cal_data_type: float32 · point at the npy dir

RDK Classroom 2-05
Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · yaml→featuremap15 / 34
YAML key fields: featuremap and no_preprocess; layout NCHW; cal type float32; plus onnx_model, shape, march, and the cal directory.

Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · Two-board Fields16 / 34
Comparison table. Speak row by row: march is bayes-e vs nash-e; opset and OE tools differ; X5 artifact is bin, S100 is hbm; keep cal dirs separate. [Read] bayes-e / nash-e = arch name + pause + letter.
Runtime

Stock Sample NV12 only

A feature-map Model Zoo artifact will not drop into the stock ultralytics_yolo runtime—use other verify tools.

  • ✕FM artifact → stock Sample: will not connect
  • ✓Verify with hrt_model_exec or hbm_runtime
  • !Legacy APIs are weak on featuremap · details in 2-06
RDK Classroom 2-05
Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · Sample Hard Limit17 / 34
Hard limit must be said: do not drop a feature-map artifact into stock Sample; on board use hrt_model_exec or hbm_runtime; inference API details are left for two-point-oh-six.

Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · X5-FM On Board21 / 34
X5 feature map on board. model_info should show input F32 from DDR. This round’s PR19 rebuild, fed divide-by-two-fifty-five only: Infer thirty-one point three one six milliseconds; all six heads vs ORT cosine at least zero point nine nine one; decode yields eight detections on the same image and thresholds as ORT. This is a single-image input-domain loop, not an mAP or full accuracy verification. The old twenty-six point seven three nine millisecond anchor was the pre-fix zero-to-two-fifty-five cal domain—do not present it as current FM.

NV12

From feature map change three

Swap cal, re-run OE; once green, remaining gaps should mostly be preprocess
RDK Classroom 2-05
Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · Three Fields → NV1226 / 34
First recall feature map: types, layout, no preprocess, float32 calibration. Field 1: input_type_rt to nv12. Field 2: input_type_train to rgb. Field 3: norm to data_scale, and swap the calibration images. X5 is packed NV12; S100 is Y and UV split. After the change, swap calibration and re-run OE; once it works, remaining gaps should mostly be preprocess. YAML fields follow conversion/. [Read] NV12—never NVR; bayes-e / nash-e = arch + pause + letter.
data_scale

Use data_scale ≈1/255 · cal per board

ptq_nv12_{x5,s100}.yaml; YAML data_scale≈1/255 (not mean+scale). X5 on-disk 0..255 + mapper HzPreprocess; S100 on-disk /255, calibrate sees 0..1, then insert_image_preprocess at quantize—data_scale is for runtime, not a second /255.

ItemX5 NV12S100 NV12
YAMLptq_nv12_x5ptq_nv12_s100
rt / trainnv12 / rgbnv12 / rgb
norm · scaledata_scale · 1/255data_scale · 1/255
cal rangergb_f32 0..255s100_npy /255
shapepacked NV12Y + UV
RDK Classroom 2-05
Self-train YOLO · feature map → NV12 · YAML · NV12 Side-by-side27 / 34
NV12 side-by-side: rt to nv12, train to rgb; YAML uses data_scale about one over two-fifty-five—not data_mean_and_scale. X5: on-disk zero-to-two-fifty-five rgbchw, then mapper HzPreprocess. S100: on-disk already /255 npy; compile calibrates on 0..1, then inserts image preprocess at quantize; YAML data_scale is for runtime—not a second divide at cal time. Do not reuse the old X5 featuremap zero-to-two-fifty-five story for NV12 or FM. X5 packed; S100 Y+UV. YAML follows conversion/. [Read] NV12—never NVR.
